item.case_name: A one-minute explainer with a fixed sequence of facts: the citric acid cycle
item.title: Citric acid cycle, a 60 s explainer

turns.text: Make a 60-second widescreen explainer video on the citric acid cycle (the Krebs cycle) for first-year biology students. Show the cycle as a loop inside a mitochondrion: acetyl-CoA enters and joins oxaloacetate to form citrate, two carbons leave as CO2, NADH, FADH2 and ATP are produced along the way, and oxaloacetate is regenerated so the loop starts again. Label the key molecules on screen as they appear, under the title 'Citric acid cycle'. Calm English narration explaining each step as it happens. Simple clean 2D animation, no music.

stages.text:
Citric acid cycle
kind: explainer
style: Widescreen, clean 2D animation with readable molecule labels, calm English narration explaining each reaction, and no music.
0–6 seconds: Under “Citric acid cycle,” an oval mitochondrial cutaway reveals the outer membrane, folded inner membrane and matrix. Calm English narration introduces the reaction diagram.

6–13 seconds: Labeled acetyl-CoA enters the diagram, not across the membrane; its two-carbon acetyl group joins four-carbon oxaloacetate, forming six-carbon citrate and releasing coenzyme A.

13–18 seconds: Citrate rearranges into labeled isocitrate without carbon loss.

18–25 seconds: Isocitrate becomes five-carbon α-ketoglutarate; labels mark the first CO₂ and NADH.

25–32 seconds: α-Ketoglutarate becomes four-carbon succinyl-CoA, releasing the second CO₂ and producing a second NADH. Neither departing CO₂ is tracked from the incoming acetyl pair.

32–38 seconds: Succinyl-CoA becomes succinate; ATP appears with the small qualification “GTP in some tissues.”

38–44 seconds: Beside the inner membrane, succinate becomes fumarate; enzyme-bound FAD becomes FADH₂ and stays bound.

44–52 seconds: Water is added to fumarate, forming malate. Malate is oxidized, regenerating oxaloacetate and producing the third NADH to close the loop.

52–60 seconds: Hold the loop with totals per acetyl-CoA: 2 CO₂, 3 NADH, 1 FADH₂, 1 ATP equivalent. Narration explains that reduced carriers supply electrons for subsequent ATP production.
stages.note: research: Citric acid cycle — research for one complete turn, shown inside a mitochondrion in 60 seconds. This is a biochemical episode, not a historical reenactment; no people, buildings or vessels are needed. Dates below are source publication dates, not dates when the reactions occurred.

items.prompt: Widescreen clean 2D animation, with flat colors, readable molecule labels, and gentle continuous movement. The voice is warm, unhurried, and neutral in accent. 0–2 s: On a pale background, show an oval mitochondrial cutaway with a teal outer membrane, a darker folded inner membrane, and a cream matrix. At top center, display "Citric acid cycle" in large dark sans-serif lettering; retain this title throughout the film. 2–6 s: Gently enlarge the cutaway without cutting. Brief leader lines identify "Outer membrane", "Inner membrane", and "Matrix". In the matrix, a faint circular arrow guide appears, clearly a reaction diagram rather than an anatomical structure. Leave a visible inner-membrane fold beside its lower-left edge. A calm adult English narrator says exactly: "In eukaryotes, the citric acid cycle occurs in the mitochondrial matrix." Use only restrained, quiet animation sounds beneath the voice. No other text, no cuts, no music, no subtitles.
